title: A page for people leaving ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini

steps.intro: Mark what holds and what doesn't. Nothing is designed yet.

steps.headline: Its readers already use ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, or are searching for DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen or similar, and are open to something else.
steps.changed: They arrive from a search ('chatgpt alternative' is about 110,000 US searches a month; 'deepseek vs chatgpt' 12,100), an ad, AlternativeTo or a comparison article. They know what an AI assistant is; they don't know youcoded.
steps.notice: The page assumes they already like AI and skips explaining it, unlike the homepage, which has to start from zero.

steps.headline: In the first seconds they learn they can keep the AI they like, or try others, and get an app that becomes theirs.
steps.changed: Built on the marketing takes made for this same audience ('Make it mine', 'Purple is the new orange'): 'make anything you can imagine, just by asking' and 'stop waiting for updates'. Customize and make it yours, never 'build your own app'; home and money pages only as examples.
steps.notice: The top reads like the continuation of those ads, so someone who saw one and searched lands somewhere familiar.

steps.headline: Each app they might be leaving gets its own short section, tuned to what that app does well and badly.
steps.changed: ChatGPT (price tiers, its huge app directory conceded), Claude (Cowork and the new install-as-app feature, conceded and answered), Gemini (Google's three-year keeping of reviewed chats), and the open models (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax), each with its own facts and dated sources.
steps.notice: A ChatGPT user and a DeepSeek user read different sections of the same page; neither has to read about the other's app.

steps.headline: Privacy is said exactly: youcoded never receives your messages, but a cloud model's company does; truly private means a model on your own computer.
steps.changed: Checked in the app's code on 2026-11-28: it does not choose which companies OpenRouter routes your requests to, so we can't promise DeepSeek through youcoded avoids China. Also no comparison tables, and the not-affiliated sentence (brand guide).
steps.notice: Some sentences are less punchy than a rival's would be, but none can be knocked down in a comment thread.

steps.headline: Every picture on the page is a real recording of the app, as on the homepage.
steps.changed: The landing page's rule: clips come from the real app, filmed by our recording tools, never drawn. You allowed faked scenes for ads; this page follows the website's rule unless you say otherwise.
steps.notice: Clips show only what today's download does.

steps.intro: Scope decisions in words. Layout comes later, as drawings.

steps.headline: One page with a section per app, or a main page plus a short page per app?
steps.today: The site is one page. Google ranks one page best for one kind of search, and 'chatgpt alternative' and 'deepseek app' are different kinds.
steps.checked: Search volumes: Google Ads US monthly averages via seodata.dev, read 2026-11-28; app facts from youcoded source the same day.
steps.problem: One page is simpler and keeps everything together, but a DeepSeek searcher may land on a page that opens with ChatGPT. Separate pages match each search better but each must stay short and unique, as you asked.
steps.proposal: Pick a shape; either way the top promise is shared and each app's part is written for that app.

options.label: One page, sections per app
pros: Strong for the big 'chatgpt alternative' search.
cons: Weaker for model-name searches like DeepSeek or Kimi.

options.label: Main page + a short page per app
pros: Each search lands on its own app's page first.
DeepSeek's privacy story gets the room it needs.
cons: Five or six short pages to keep accurate.
Each has to earn its place, or it gets cut.

steps.headline: What do we tell people searching DeepSeek, many of whom worry their data goes to China?
steps.today: DeepSeek's own privacy policy says it stores data on servers in China. Pages answering 'use DeepSeek without sending data to China' are mostly old how-tos that need typing commands.
steps.checked: DeepSeek privacy policy dated 2025-02-14 and youcoded's code, both read 2026-11-28.
steps.problem: youcoded can reach DeepSeek's models through OpenRouter, but doesn't control which company serves them. Full DeepSeek is too big for a normal computer; smaller open models like Qwen run offline in youcoded.
steps.proposal: Pick what the DeepSeek part says.

options.label: Offline open models
options.summary: Use DeepSeek through OpenRouter if you like; for real privacy, run an open model like Qwen on your own computer, no commands.
pros: Answers the worry better than the how-tos: no terminal.
cons: Not literally DeepSeek offline (too big for most computers).

options.label: Also add a privacy setting
options.summary: Same as above now, and a new app setting later that tells OpenRouter to use only providers that don't keep your data.
pros: Lets the page say more, once built.
cons: New app work; it would go through its own design first.

options.label: Don't mention privacy
cons: Ignores the main reason many of them search.
